newsitem.title: USA: Western Resources seeks earlier ADT meeting.
newsitem.headline: Western Resources seeks earlier ADT meeting.

text.p: Western Resources Inc., pressing its $3.5 billion hostile takeover bid for ADT Ltd., said Tuesday it has asked a federal court in Florida to order the security services powerhouse to hold a special shareholders meeting no later than March 20.
Western Resources said it opposed ADT's plans to hold a special meeting July 8.

In papers filed Monday with the U.S. District Court in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., Western Resources said there was no reason to delay the meeting other than the ADT board's "desire to interfere with shareholder voting rights and to extend their stay in office as long as possible."
Western Resources, a Topeka, Kan.-based natural gas and electric company which holds a 27.1 percent state in ADT, is seeking to replace ADT's board of directors.
Earlier this month, Boca Raton, Fla.-based ADT -- North America's largest security services company -- contended a merger with Western would stymie its growth prospects.
In a proxy statement to shareholders, ADT said it would be open to the transaction but maintained the $3.5 billion takeover attempt by the Kansas utility was full of risks.
The cash and stock transaction values ADT at about $22.50 a share.
ADT stock was unchanged at $22.75 Tuesday afternoon on the New York Stock Exchange, while Western Resources rose 25 cents to $31.25.

ADT provides continuous monitoring of commercial and residential security systems to more than 1.7 million customers. It is also the nation's second-largest provider of vehicle auction services, with 27 auction centres.
Western Resources provides natural gas service to about 650,000 customers in Kansas and Oklahoma and electricity to some 600,000 customers.

ADT was slated to be acquired last year by Republic Industries Inc. in a transaction that valued it at about $29 a share, but the deal fell apart due to uncertainty over Republic's volatile stock price.
